                                         ABSTRACT                                                                                        1    INTRODUCTION
                                         We report on Just-in-Time catching test generation at Meta, de-                                 Most work on unit test generation [6, 9, 18, 26, 34, 45, 50, 59, 61] is
                                         signed to prevent bugs in large scale backend systems of hundreds                               concerned with ‘hardening’ tests. That is, tests that pass at gener-
                                         of millions of line of code. Unlike traditional hardening tests, which                          ation time, and land into the code base to ‘harden’ against future
                                         pass at generation time, catching tests are meant to fail, surfac-                              regressions. By contrast, ‘catching’ tests fail at test generation time

                                         CCS CONCEPTS                                                                                       A weak catch is simply one that fails on the current revision,
                                                                                                                                         whereas a strong catch is one that also should fail (a true positive
                                         • Software and its engineering → Software testing and debug-
                                                                                                                                         failure) according to this general oracle. Its failure reveals a bug in
                                         ging.
                                                                                                                                         the code under test. A strictly weak catch is a false positive failure
                                                                                                                                         that reveals a bug in the test case, including oracle misalignment.
                                         KEYWORDS                                                                                        The challenge is to determine whether a weak catch is strong. The
                                         Unit Tests, Automated Testing, LLMs, Test Oracles.                                              problem of automatically generating such strong catching tests
                                                                                                                                         Just-in-Time (JIT) as revisions are submitted, is called the ‘Catching

2     BASELINES FOR JUST IN TIME CATCHING                                 3     DIFF-AWARE WORKFLOWS
A prerequisite for any approach to generate strong catches on a           Unlike hardening workflows, a catch generation workflow can al-
diff is the ability to generate weak catches. In order to assess the      ways choose to exploit information about the diff to help it find ways
degree to which existing technologies can generate weak catches,          to make the test fail on that diff. A purpose-built catch workflow
we used three ‘baseline’ approaches, described below.                     is thus ‘diff-aware’. We have experimented with two approaches

                                                                          depicted in Figure 1). The ‘dodgy diff’ workflow is aware of the
                                                                          diff, but makes no attempt to infer anything about its intention.
                                                                          Rather, it treats the diff as if it were a mutant of its parent, implicitly

   Although coincidental catching tests generated from hardening
are rare (see Table 1), coincidental hardening test generated by         We reported experience and empirical results from mutation-guided,
catching are highly prevalent, as Table 6 shows. Therefore, one nat-     LLM-based test generation targeting risky code changes (diffs) to
ural way to approach the overall combined problems of hardening          uncover faults just before production—the Catching JiTTest Chal-
and catching test generation, is to simultaneously do both: primar-      lenge [37]. This approach has prevented severe bugs from landing
ily focussing on generating catching tests, while also harvesting        at Meta. Diff and intent awareness greatly increase the number
hardening test generated during this process.                            of weak catches found. To transition from weak to strong catches,

                                                                         man review load by 70%, with statistical analysis showing strong
8     RELATED WORK                                                       agreement with human labels.
Automated test generation has a long history, dating back to the            A key advantage is that engineers rarely need to write or review
1960s [13], and remaining active through the decades since [43].         tests, avoiding AI code quality issues [28, 30]. Tests are generated
Currently, established test generation techniques tend to use either     and assessed automatically; engineers only confirm if changes are
search-based and evolutionary approaches [10, 26, 27, 49] or Sym-        intended, with negligible impact on development velocity. When
bolic execution [15, 31, 63]. Research has led to the introduction       changes are unexpected, engineers use test code to quickly identify
of practical publicly available test generation tools such as Evo-       and fix issues. We hope these results encourage further research
Suite [26], Randoop [54] and Klee [14]. More recent studies have         on just-in-time catching test generation and provide scalable, in-
focussed on LLM-based code generators such as Codex, Copilot,            dustrially relevant baseline results for future improvements.
and Code Llama [6, 18, 45, 59, 61, 68].
   Existing tools primarily generate unit tests to improve coverage,     10    ACKNOWLEDGMENTS
but coverage may not entail fault revelation; recent research [17]       We would like to thank the leadership of Meta’s Product Compliance
shows mutation testing is more effective, leading to its practical       and Privacy, Fundamental Artificial Intelligence Research (FAIR),
adoption at Meta [25]. Whether mutation- or coverage-guided,             Developer Infrastructure (DevInfra), and Instagram Product Foun-
these approaches automate human-style unit test writing [6, 9, 18,       dation teams for supporting our work over the past decade, and
26, 34, 45, 50, 59, 61], thereby focusing on hardening rather than       the many Meta software engineers and testers whose experience,
catching test generation.                                                expertise, and engagement have helped shape the ideas presented
   By contrast, the focus of this paper is on catching unit tests        here. We would also like to thank the many academics and other
which are very different: they fail at generation time, a property       researchers with whom we have had the enormous pleasure to
they share with techniques such as fuzzing [46] and system level         interact over 3+ decades of research work on verification, testing
test generation with tools like Sapienz [7, 47]. However, unlike these   and AI.
approaches to catching bugs, we focus on generating catching tests
with respect to a general oracle rather than the implicit oracle [12].
